newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU's Van Miert sees room for deal on VW subsidies.
newsitem.headline: EU's Van Miert sees room for deal on VW subsidies.

text.p: European Union competition commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Tuesday there would be no "rotten compromises" in a thorny subsidy dispute with Volkswagen AG, but there was still room for a deal.

In an interview in the daily Die Welt, Van Miert said the German carmaker could invest more of its own money in a pair of east German car plants in order to justify government subisidies which the EU has said are anti-competitive.

The Commission is disputing the legality of 91 million marks ($58.5 million) of a 142-million-mark subsidy package the state of Saxony has granted Volkswagen to support its investment in plants there.
"Volkswagen could reduce its capacity at the plant, but that is not likely," Van Miert said. "It is therefore conceivable that more will be invested there than had previously been seen."
At issue in the debate is paragraph 92, section 2c of the Maastricht Treaty. The passage allows for government subsidies to help support German unification.
But Van Miert said that a wide interpretation of this provision could lead to a collapse of the subsidy allowances. ($ = 1.554 German Marks)
